title: Portal invitations
description: Invitations by email link (portal plan P2.2; spec §Tenancy). Firebase Auth sends and verifies the link, so an invitation here is an address, a role and a state: it holds no token — a stored token would be a list of live credentials — and it is accepted only by a verified address equal to the one it names, both sides folded by access.Member (F10). Every object here is closed, because ee/keyservice/wire_invites.go decodes it with DisallowUnknownFields.

invite.description: One invitation, as the organisation's owners and admins read it.

id.description: The invitation's id. It is what the accepting call names, and it is not a secret: what makes the invitation usable is the sign-in link Firebase Auth sends to the address.

organisation_id.description: The organisation the person is invited into. A reseller invites into a customer organisation it has already created (D2191), so this is always set: an invitation never creates an organisation.

email.description: The invited address. An invitation is accepted by a token whose verified address equals it and by no other (F10), which is why the address and not the id is the binding.

role.description: The role the membership will hold. It is chosen at the invitation because it has to exist before the person does: the operations seed invites that organisation's first owner (P2.2).

state.description: Where the invitation stands. Accepted is written at the first sign-in of the address it names, which is also the instant a membership binds to a uid (F40); expired is a pending invitation whose window has closed, which is a state and not a deletion, because a person reading the list is asking what happened.

invited_by.description: The inviter's email address: an owner reading the list is asking who asked for this, and an address is what they recognise.

created_at.description: When the invitation was created, in UTC.

expires_at.description: When the invitation stops being acceptable, in UTC. A window is what keeps a forgotten invitation to a departed colleague from being a way in months later.

accepted_at.description: When it was accepted, or null while it has not been. An invitation nobody accepted has no such instant, which is not its creation time.

create.description: An owner's or admin's request to invite somebody (P2.2). The organisation is the caller's own and is not in the body: a request that named one would be a request to invite into somebody else's.

email.description: The address to invite. For the operations organisation it must be on the domain list operations set (F9, P5.1); for a reseller's invitation the acceptance needs the SSO its own organisation needs (F40).

role.description: The role the new membership will hold.
